title: Being 'slick' with women in Kansas City
summary: Price reflects that his confidence with women gave him an image, while he always kept working.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: But, in Kansas City...I used the term "slick." I wasn't never slick, 'cause I never tried to fleece anybody, you know, or tried to sell the Brooklyn Bridge. I just would... my thing was with ladies. You know, I could make it with... you know what I mean. And really, when I come to think of it, I don't think they made too much of a contribution, I think it was just that confidence that they gave me, that made me...because I...long as I can remember, I've always worked. So I wasn't a pimp. I wasn't, you know, like, you know, had to have...live in somebody's house, or some woman had to keep me and come and bring my rent--I always worked. But I think that in my mind, I wanted to think that I was slick. Just like Eddie Barefield said, every time he ever played, that I showed up with a woman. Well, that's possibly true.
